newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 5.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Wednesday:

* Top Congressional Republicans including Speaker Newt Gingrich intensified demands that a special independent counsel be appointed to investigate Democratic fund-raising efforts by President Clinton and Vice President Al Gore.

* White House aides walk a tightrope between the business of government and the politics of it, which are separated by two laws -- the Hatch Act and a late-1800s statute prohibiting the solicitation of contributions on Federal property occupied for carrying out official duties.
* President Clinton returned to his home state of Arkansas to survey the damage done by storms that killed 25 there.
* Experts say the failure to discuss death among families with a terminally ill member adds to their pain, including unwanted medical treatments and lack of support in making difficult decisions.

* A year after Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni vowed to eliminate the insurgency in the north of his country, gangs of revolutionists and Christian fundamentalist rebels have not only survived, but have intensified their bloody campaigns.
* Warning labels on consumer products have become increasingly elaborate and embarrassingly obvious as product makers seek to avoid costly personal-injury lawsuits.

* The leader of the Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages inside the Japanese embassy in Lima, Peru, did not entirely rule out the possibility of accepting asylum in Cuba, which Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori had sought as a means to end the 77-day-old siege.
